findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption managed by the configuration.

No acl or bucket policy is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving access control to defaults and creating a risk that the bucket holding vendor data becomes publicly or broadly accessible.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this data bucket would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.

Versioning is not enabled, so object deletions or overwrites (including malicious tampering or ransomware) are unrecoverable, and force_destroy = true allows the entire bucket and contents to be deleted without safeguards.
This ledger/financial export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so sensitive exported data is not encrypted with a customer-managed or enforced default key.
No logging block is defined for the ledger bucket, leaving no record of object-level or bucket-level access for audit purposes.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed with no recovery path, undermining data integrity.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose financial data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored unencrypted by configuration.
No public access block is associated with the bucket, leaving it open to accidental public exposure through future ACL or bucket policy changes.
The runbooks bucket, which typically stores operational procedures and potentially sensitive internal details, defines no server-side encryption configuration.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so access to operational runbooks is not auditable.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guarding this bucket against public ACLs or policies.
The audit trail bucket itself has no logging target configured, so tampering with or access to the central log store is not itself logged.

findings.issue_category: log bucket destroyable / no MFA delete
findings.description: force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows the entire audit history to be deleted along with the bucket, and no MFA delete is configured, weakening log integrity guarantees.
No public access block protects the audit log bucket, which uses the log-delivery-write ACL; audit logs could be exposed if a public policy or ACL is later applied.

The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption attribute into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so potentially sensitive vendor data is stored unencrypted.
